{{nihongo|'''Tsurugitachi Iwato Kowake No Mikoto Shrine'''|劒刀石床別命神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Izu Province]].

'''Tsurugitachi Iwatokowake-no-Mikoto Shrine''' (つるぎたちいわとこわけのみことじんじゃ<ref>Name and reading from [http://shizuoka-jinjacho.or.jp/shokai/jinja.php?id=4402023 Tsurugitachi Iwatokowake-no-Mikoto Shrine] (Shizuoka Prefectural Association of Shinto Shrines).</ref>, also written '''Ken-tō Iwatoko-wake-no-Mikoto Shrine''') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} in Yata, {{ill|Mishima, Shizuoka|Q653478|qid=Q653478}}, {{ill|Shizuoka Prefecture|Q131320|qid=Q131320}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}, and under the former {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|lt=shrine ranking system}} its rank was {{ill|Son-sha|Q134917284|qid=Q134917284}}.

== Enshrined deities ==
The two enshrined deities are as follows{{Sfn|Mishima City History Vol. 2|1988|p=561}}.
* Tsurugitachi Iwatokowake-no-Mikoto (つるぎたちいわとこわけのみこと)
* {{ill|Yamato Takeru|Q461258|qid=Q461258|lt=Yamato Takeru-no-Mikoto}} (やまとたけるのみこと)
*: The origin of enshrining Yamato Takeru is unknown; it is presumed to derive from eastern expedition legends of Yamato Takeru{{Sfn|Shikinaisha Survey Report|1981}}.

== History ==
== Foundation ==
Shrine tradition says that worship of waterfalls called "First Falls," "Second Falls," and "Third Falls" was the origin of this shrine{{Sfn|Mishima City History Vol. 2|1988|p=561}}. The second and third falls were lost when the railway was laid, but the first falls remain in Takekura, Mishima (old name: Takekura){{Sfn|Mishima City History Vol. 2|1988|p=561}}. Another tradition says worship began from water springing from the "sword-like stone bed" at that Takekura site{{Sfn|Shikinaisha Survey Report|1981}}.

The plateau behind the shrine, now divided by a road, was formerly continuous with the shrine grounds, and ancient tomb groups have been confirmed on that plateau{{Sfn|Mishima City History Vol. 2|1988|p=561}}. From this, it is inferred that ritual worship was conducted here since the Kofun period{{Sfn|Shikinaisha Survey Report|1981}}.

== Overview ==
In the {{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=Engi}} 5 ({{ill|927|ab|927|af|927|am|927 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|927|ar|927|ary|927|ast|927|avk|927|az|927|azb|۹۲۷ (میلادی)|bar|927|bcl|927|be|927|be_x_old|927|bg|927|bn|৯২৭|bpy|মারি ৯২৭|br|927|bs|927.|ca|927|cdo|927 nièng|ceb|927|ckb|٩٢٧|crh|927|cs|927|csb|927|cv|927|cy|927|da|927|de|927|el|927|eml|927|eo|927|es|927|et|927|eu|927|fa|۹۲۷ (میلادی)|fi|927|fo|927|fr|927|fy|927|ga|927|gan|927年|gd|927|gl|927|he|927|hi|927|hr|927.|ht|927 (almanak jilyen)|hu|927|hy|927|id|927|ilo|927|io|927|is|927|it|927|ja|927年|jv|927|ka|927|kaa|927|kk|927 жыл|ko|927년|la|927|lb|927|lij|927|lmo|927|lt|927 m.|lv|927. gads|map_bms|927|mdf|927|mg|927|mhr|927|mi|927|mk|927|mr|इ.स. ९२७|mrj|927 и|ms|927|mzn|۹۲۷|nah|927|nap|927|nds|927|new|सन् ९२७|nl|927|nn|927|no|927|nrm|927|nso|927|oc|927|or|୯୨୭|os|927-æм аз|pl|927|pnb|927|pt|927|qu|927|ro|927|ru|927 год|rue|927|sa|९२७|scn|927|sd|927ع|se|927|sh|927.|shn|927|si|927|sk|927|smn|927|sq|927|sr|927|su|927|sv|927|sw|927|tg|Соли 927|th|พ.ศ. 1470|tk|927|tl|927|tly|927|tr|927|tt|927 ел|uk|927|ur|927ء|uz|927|vec|927|vi|927|war|927|wuu|927年|xmf|927|zh|927年|zh_min_nan|927 nî|zh_yue|927年|qid=Q30470}}) {{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}} {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932}}, the shikinaisha "Ken-tō Iwatoko-wake-no-Mikoto Shrine" in {{ill|Tagata District, Shizuoka|Q1154841|qid=Q1154841}}, {{ill|Izu Province|Q860928|qid=Q860928}}, is identified with this shrine{{Sfn|Place Names of Shizuoka Prefecture|2000}}. However, documentary evidence showing this identification descends only to a munafuda from {{ill|Bunki|Q1324885|qid=Q1324885}} 2 ({{ill|1502|Q6137|qid=Q6137}}){{Sfn|Shikinaisha Survey Report|1981}}. If this shrine is that shikinaisha, the stone beds and cliffs of the first, second, and third falls are said to represent the "sword/blade stone bed"{{Sfn|Shikinaisha Survey Report|1981}}. The reading is annotated "Tsurugitachi Iwatoko" in the Kujō family manuscript, while other manuscripts give "Kemutono Iwatoko"{{Sfn|Shikinaisha Survey Report|1981}}.

In medieval {{ill|Izu no Kuni Shinkai-chō|Q17193087|qid=Q17193087}}, the entry "Junior Fourth Rank Upper, Takiyama no Myōjin"{{Sfn|Place Names of Shizuoka Prefecture|2000}} or "Junior Fourth Rank Upper, Natsume no Myōjin"{{Sfn|Shikinaisha Survey Report|1981}}{{Sfn|Mishima City History Vol. 2|1988|p=561}} is identified with this shrine.

By the late medieval period it had syncretized with mountain ascetic worship, {{ill|Shugendō|Q1483875|qid=Q1483875}}, and was also called "Ontake Daigongen"{{Sfn|Shikinaisha Survey Report|1981}}. Other detailed history is unclear, but the shrine preserves munafuda from {{ill|Bunki|Q1324885|qid=Q1324885}}, {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}}, {{ill|Genbun|Q1145754|qid=Q1145754}}, {{ill|Bunsei|Q1327119|qid=Q1327119}}, {{ill|Kaei|Q1146125|qid=Q1146125}}, etc., and displays a torii plaque from {{ill|Meiwa|Q1146161|qid=Q1146161}}{{Sfn|Mishima City History Vol. 2|1988|p=561}}.

In {{ill|Meiji era|ar|فترة مييجي|ast|Dómina Meiji|az|Meydzi dövrü|azb|مئی‌جی دؤورو|be|Перыяд Мэйдзі|bn|মেইজি যুগ|bo|མེའི་ཇིའི་དུས་དུས་མཚམས།|ca|Era Meiji|cs|Období Meidži|da|Meiji-perioden|de|Meiji-Zeit|el|Μεϊτζί (περίοδος)|es|Era Meiji|et|Meiji periood|eu|Meiji Aroa|fa|دوره میجی|fi|Meiji-kausi|fr|Ère Meiji|gl|Período Meiji|he|תקופת מייג'י|hr|Meiji (razdoblje)|ht|Epòk Meiji|hu|Meidzsi-kor|id|Zaman Meiji|io|Ero Meiji|is|Meiji-tímabilið|it|Periodo Meiji|ja|明治|ka|მეიძის ეპოქა|kbp|Mejii wɛɛ yaa alɩwaatʊ|kk|Мэйдзи дәуірі|ko|메이지 시대|la|Aetas Meiji|lt|Meidži laikotarpis|lv|Meidzi periods|mk|Меиџи (период)|mn|Мэйжийн эрин|ms|Zaman Meiji|nl|Meijiperiode|nn|Meiji|no|Meiji-perioden|pl|Meiji (okres)|pt|Era Meiji|ro|Perioada Meiji|ru|Мэйдзи|simple|Meiji period|sk|Obdobie Meidži|sq|Periudha Meixhi|sr|Меиџи период|sv|Meijiperioden|ta|மெய்சி காலம்|th|ยุคเมจิ|tl|Panahong Meiji|tr|Meiji Dönemi|uk|Період Мейдзі|ur|میجی دور|vi|Thời kỳ Minh Trị|war|Panahon Meiji|wuu|明治|zh|明治|zh_classical|明治|zh_min_nan|Bêng-tī|zh_yue|明治|qid=Q3125096}} 6 ({{ill|1873|Q7757|qid=Q7757}}), it was ranked as a {{ill|Son-sha|Q134917284|qid=Q134917284}} in the modern shrine ranking system{{Sfn|Shikinaisha Survey Report|1981}}. During the Meiji separation of Shinto and Buddhism, this shrine was called "Ontake Shrine," but in {{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}} 23 ({{ill|1948|Q5165|qid=Q5165}}) it was renamed to the present "Tsurugitachi Iwatokowake-no-Mikoto Shrine"{{Sfn|Shikinaisha Survey Report|1981}}. It is also colloquially called "Yata Gomonsha"{{Sfn|Shikinaisha Survey Report|1981}}.

== Divine rank ==
* Junior Fourth Rank Upper (''{{ill|Izu no Kuni Shinkai-chō|Q17193087|qid=Q17193087}}'') - "Takiyama no Myōjin"{{Sfn|Place Names of Shizuoka Prefecture|2000}} or "Natsume no Myōjin"{{Sfn|Mishima City History Vol. 2|1988|p=561}}.

== Festivals ==
Rites are held on {{ill|January 15|Q2260|qid=Q2260}} and {{ill|October 15|Q2919|qid=Q2919}}{{Sfn|Mishima City History Vol. 2|1988|p=561}}; the latter is the annual festival<ref name="board">Explanatory board in the precincts.</ref>.
